problems.memo_sentence: "The authors use QAOA as a hybrid quantum–classical algorithm optimized with the classical COBYLA method, and systematically compare three constraint-encoding strategies: quadratization/QUBO with an X-mixer and QUBO-to-Ising mapping, penalty dephasing that separates return and penalty with a weight-adder, constraint flag, penalty phase, and ancilla reinitialization, and a Quantum Zeno-inspired approach that repeatedly measures a flag qubit to confine evolution to a feasible subspace via a projected Hamiltonian without post-selection."
problems.source_evidence: "In this work, we used Constrained Optimization BY Linear Approximation (COBYLA) algorithm designed in scipy library." and "We use quantum Fourier transform (QFT) adder to add weight for all senario." and "For implementation, We use quantum Fourier transform (QFT) adder to add weight for all senario. [19]"
problems.explanation: The memo presents the QFT adder and several circuit components as if they are part of this paper's own method, but the paper explicitly cites prior work for the adder construction and related penalty-dephasing ideas. This is a case of attributing externally sourced techniques to the paper itself.

problems.explanation: The memo mentions the absence of post-selection but omits the paper's explicit rationale that post-selection would dramatically increase shot count and affect runtime and accuracy. That limitation is central to why the Zeno method was implemented this way.
